# Audit schema v1

Every audit record is an OTLP LogRecord with EventName `audit` and the
attributes below, and no others (the closed set). Go writers spell keys
through the generated `audit.Key*` constants and test their records with
`audit.Check` and `audittest`; other writers use `cmd/auditschema`.

## Writers

| writer | code | who |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | H | A request a component served for a caller, recorded by that component: snowplow for a person's or an agent's request, authn for a login and a /delegate token. |
| `gateway` | G | The agent gateway's hop record, projected by the collector. |
| `action` | T | An agent's per-action record, written by whatever performs the action. |
| `controller` | C | A controller reconcile. |

## Levels

- **R**: required. **R (mark)**: required, or omitted and named in
  `krateo.audit.incomplete` when the writer cannot establish it.
- **C: when**: required when *when* holds. **[checked]**: `Check` evaluates the
  condition on the record. Without it, the condition is not visible on the
  record and `Check` treats the key as optional, unless it is **(mark)**: then
  it must be present or marked.
- **O**: optional. **NE**: not established by this writer, never written.
  **—**: does not apply.

## Keys

| key | type | semconv | H | G | T | C | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## The target rule

Every record names its target: `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource` (a Kubernetes object) or `server.address`
(an external endpoint), and, for a writer that lists more, one of its own
target keys (`url.path`, a non-resource path, for the request writer).
Marker `target`.

| writer | targets | of the keys |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | exactly one | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource`, `server.address`, `url.path` |
| `gateway` | exactly one | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource`, `server.address` |
| `action` | exactly one | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource`, `server.address` |
| `controller` | at least one | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource`, `server.address` |

## Credential targets

A key marked **never on a credential target** is not written on a record whose
Kubernetes target, as `object_ref` names it, is one of these; `Check`
reports it there as `not-for-target`. A target with no subresource
listed matches the resource and every subresource of it.

| api_group | resource | subresource |
|---|---|---|
| core (omitted) | `secrets` | any |
| core (omitted) | `serviceaccounts` | `token` |
| `authentication.k8s.io` | `tokenreviews` | any |

## Conditions `Check` evaluates

- `k8s_target`: The record names a Kubernetes object: k8s.namespace.name or any krateo.audit.object_ref.* key is present.
- `write`: krateo.audit.verb is a write: create, update, patch, delete, deletecollection (a Kubernetes object), post or put (anything else).
- `method_other`: http.request.method is _OTHER: the writer was given a method semconv does not name.
- `delegated`: The record carries a delegation: krateo.audit.delegation or krateo.audit.on_behalf_of.user.name is present.
- `impersonated`: The record carries an impersonation: either krateo.audit.impersonated_user.* key is present.
- `caused`: The record names the object a controller reconciled: any krateo.audit.cause_ref.* key is present.
- `denied`: krateo.audit.outcome is denied: the writer itself refused.
- `content_write`: krateo.audit.verb creates or replaces an object's content: create or update.
- `client_rejected`: The writer rejected the client's provenance header: krateo.audit.client.rejected is present.
- `client_provenance`: The record carries provenance the client asserted: a krateo.audit.client.* key other than source and rejected is present.
- `confirmed_set`: The record names the confirmed set its write belongs to: any krateo.audit.client.confirmed_set.* key is present.
- `endpoint_target`: The record's target is an external endpoint: server.address is present.
- `succeeded`: krateo.audit.outcome is success: the authority answered and the action completed.
- `kept_existing_value`: krateo.audit.denial_reason is kept_existing_value: the writer declined to overwrite an authorization-bearing value already present.
- `public_actor`: krateo.audit.actor_class is public: the request carried no credential at all, and the writer served it as its configured public identity.
- `issued_or_audience_refused`: krateo.audit.outcome is success, or krateo.audit.denial_reason is audience_not_allowed: a token exchange that issued its token, or that refused the requested audience.

## Formats `Check` enforces

A value that breaks its key's format is `bad-format`; an int below its
minimum, or not below its `less_than` key, is `out-of-range`.

- `delegation_link` (`audit.ValidDelegationLink`): `<class>:<subject>`, the class one of the actor classes or empty, the subject not empty.
- `marker_list` (`audit.ValidMarkerList`): comma-separated markers of the schema, each at most once.
- `sha256_hex` (`audit.ValidSHA256Hex`): 64 lowercase hex digits. Pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`.
- `content_hash` (`audit.ValidContentHash`): `c1:` and 64 lowercase hex digits: the content hash in form c1 (below). Any other form prefix is refused: a stored hash is read only with the form that made it.
- `uuid` (`audit.ValidUUID`): a UUID in its canonical textual form, lowercase (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits). Pattern `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`.
- `opaque_id` (`audit.ValidOpaqueID`): 1 to 128 of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. Pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`.
- `session_id` (`audit.ValidSessionID`): 1 to 128 of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`: a correlation id safe in W3C baggage and on a log line. The shape snowplow, the id's origin, accepts and mints (audit#32): its minted ids, a trace id, a UUID all fit. Pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`.
- `k8s_namespace` (`audit.ValidK8sNamespace`): a Kubernetes namespace name: a DNS-1123 label, 1 to 63 of `[a-z0-9-]`, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Pattern `^([a-z0-9]|[a-z0-9][-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])$`.
- `endpoint_ref_name` (`audit.ValidEndpointRefName`): the name of the Secret an endpointRef names: 1 to 253 of `[a-z0-9.-]`, starting and ending with a letter or digit, and never a per-user clientconfig Secret's name (one ending in `-clientconfig` or `-clientconfig-stepup`), which embeds a username.
- `url_path` (`audit.ValidURLPath`): a URL path: `/` and up to 1000 more characters, no query, no fragment, no whitespace. Pattern `^/[^?#\s]{0,1000}$`.
- `rfc3339` (`audit.ValidRFC3339`): an RFC 3339 timestamp, with or without fractional seconds.
- `identity_claim` (`audit.ValidIdentityClaim`): authn's claim of a verified identity, `["<strategy>","<issuer>","<subject>"]`, exactly as authn's storage.EncodeClaim writes it (Go's encoding/json rendering of the three strings, so the value an admin writes to the authn.krateo.io/claim annotation is the same string): the strategy one of authn's sign-in strategies (basic, ldap, oauth, oidc, serviceaccount), the subject not empty.
- `token_audience` (`audit.ValidTokenAudience`): the audience a token is issued for, a recipient's name: a DNS-1123 subdomain (1 to 253 of `[a-z0-9.-]`, dot-separated labels each starting and ending with a letter or digit), or an absolute `https://` URI with a host and no userinfo, query or fragment, all printable ASCII.

## Closed values per writer and per action

A key whose values depend on the writer lists them per writer class. `Check`
reports any other value as `bad-enum`, and the key on a writer class that
declares none as `not-for-writer`. A key whose values depend on the
record's `krateo.action` lists them per action, within a writer class:
`Check` reports a value outside the set of the record's action as
`bad-enum`, and the key on a record whose action declares no set
(`krateo.action` absent included) as `not-for-action`. A writer or an action
gains a value in a minor release, by adding it to `schema/v1.yaml`. Go
writers spell each value through its generated constant.

## `krateo.action` literals

`krateo.action` is the emit site's own literal. Schema v1 does not enforce
its values: `Check` accepts any non-empty literal.
The only rule that reads it is a per-action closed set (above): `krateo.audit.check_result` on `authn.username.check`.
The literals below are registered so that writers spell the same action the
same way and readers can query by it. A writer registers a literal by adding
it here, in `internal/schemagen/doc.go`; every action a per-action set
declares must be registered.

| writer | literal | the action |
|---|---|---|
| `controller` | `helm.install` | helm installs a release that does not exist yet (cdc's Create, no release) |
| `controller` | `helm.upgrade` | helm upgrades an existing release (cdc's Create, a release exists) |
| `controller` | `helm.reconcile` | helm reconciles a release to its desired state: Observe's self-heal or Update, through plumbing's Reconcile, a three-way merge that patches drift and prunes children |
| `controller` | `helm.rollback` | helm rolls a release back: Observe clearing a release stuck pending past the grace, and Delete's rollback; real child patches, creates and deletes (plumbing#140 per-child verdicts) |
| `controller` | `helm.uninstall` | helm uninstalls a release (cdc's Delete) |
| `controller` | `rbac.apply` | a controller creates or updates RBAC: Roles, ClusterRoles, their bindings and ServiceAccounts. Emitted today by core-provider (core-provider@b1f9b5f): a composition's ServiceAccount, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, Role and RoleBinding (`tools/deploy/deploy.go:225-271`, `installRBACResources`), the credentials Secret's Role and RoleBinding (`deploy.go:450`, `:474`, `Deploy`), the RESTAction read-set ClusterRole and binding (`restactionrbac.go:148`, `:152`, `applyRestActionRBAC`), the chart-inspector RBAC projected onto a spoke (`chartinspector.go:110-131`, `ProjectChartInspector`), and a derived binding re-subjected to a new ServiceAccount (`resubject.go:119`, `ResubjectDerivedRBAC`). oasgen-provider will write it too (oasgen-provider#543; no emit site yet) |
| `controller` | `rbac.delete` | a controller deletes RBAC, the same kinds. Emitted today by core-provider (core-provider@b1f9b5f): a composition's set (`tools/deploy/deploy.go:376-408`, `uninstallRBACResources`), the credentials Secret's Role and RoleBinding (`deploy.go:806`, `:820`, `Undeploy`), the chart-inspector RBAC on a spoke (`chartinspector.go:301`, `DeleteProjectedChartInspector`), and dangling controller bindings with the roles no other binding references (`danglingrbac.go:204`, `:244`, `RemoveDanglingControllerBindings`). oasgen-provider will write it too (oasgen-provider#543; no emit site yet) |
| `controller` | `secret.apply` | core-provider copies a Secret the chart-inspector pod references from the hub onto a spoke (core-provider@b1f9b5f, `tools/deploy/chartinspector.go:220`, `projectPodRefs`) |
| `controller` | `authn.mapping.apply` | core-provider applies an authn ServiceAccount mapping (`serviceaccount.authn.krateo.io`, core-provider@b1f9b5f): a composition's apiRef mapping (`tools/deploy/authnmapping.go:121`, `applyAuthnServiceAccountMapping`) and core-provider's own singleton mapping (`:170`, `ensureSelfAuthnMapping`) |
| `controller` | `composition.mirror` | core-provider mirrors a hub Composition onto its spoke (core-provider@b1f9b5f): creates or updates the spoke copy (`controllers/compositionmirror/compositionmirror.go:634`, `:678`, `mirrorDown`) and deletes a spoke mirror with no hub counterpart (`:751`, `garbageCollect`) |
| `controller` | `composition.hub.delete` | core-provider deletes every hub Composition of a remote CompositionDefinition being deleted (core-provider@b1f9b5f, `controllers/compositionmirror/compositionmirror.go:303`, `:372`, `reconcileDelete` through `deleteAllHubCompositions`) |
| `controller` | `composition.migrate` | core-provider moves a Composition to a CompositionDefinition's new version, relabelled and written through the new version's endpoint (core-provider@b1f9b5f, `controllers/compositiondefinitions/helpers/getters/getters.go:381`, `UpdateCompositionsVersion` through `updateCompositionWithRetry`) |
| `request` | `authn.username.check` | authn's `POST /usernames/check`, whether a username is free; its result is `krateo.audit.check_result` |
| `request` | `debug.shadowParity` | snowplow's `POST /debug/shadow-parity`, which toggles a per-process dark parity measurement; its target is the non-resource path, `url.path` (v0.12.0) |

## A controller row: the object written and the object reconciled

A controller row has two objects. `krateo.audit.object_ref.*` (with
`k8s.namespace.name`) is the object the controller **wrote**, as the
apiserver's `objectRef` of that write names it. `krateo.audit.cause_ref.*` is
the object it **reconciled**: the custom resource whose reconcile made the
write. Write `cause_ref` on every row of a reconcile, also when the object
written is the reconciled resource itself (its status, its finalizers), so
that a reader joins on `cause_ref` alone. A write to an external endpoint
names the endpoint in `server.address` and the resource in `cause_ref`.
Only a controller writes `cause_ref`; for every other writer it does not
apply (`not-for-writer`). Once a row names a cause, its
`api_version`, `resource`, `name` and `uid` are required.

### The snowplow join

A person's write reaches a controller through the object it wrote. snowplow's
request row carries that object's `krateo.audit.object_ref.uid` and
`krateo.audit.object_ref.generation` as the apiserver returned them; the
row of a reconcile of that generation carries the same pair as
`krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid` and `krateo.audit.cause_ref.generation`.
The join reaches the request's `session.id` without touching the object:

```sql
SELECT h.LogAttributes['session.id']    AS session,
       c.ScopeName                      AS controller,
       c.LogAttributes['krateo.action'] AS action,
       c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.outcome'] AS outcome
FROM default.krateo_audit AS c
INNER JOIN default.krateo_audit AS h
   ON h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.uid'] = c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid']
  AND h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation'] = c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.generation']
WHERE h.ScopeName = 'github.com/krateo-platformops/snowplow/audit'
  AND c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid'] != ''
  AND h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation'] != ''
```

A DELETE's request row carries no generation (the apiserver returns none for
a delete), so a reconcile a delete caused joins on `uid` alone. A
controller row written before v0.5.0 carries no `cause_ref`: it named the
object it reconciled in `object_ref`, so a join that spans those rows reads
`cause_ref` where it is set and `object_ref` otherwise.

### Writes a reconcile coalesced: the generation range join

`krateo.audit.cause_ref.generation` is the generation the controller
**reconciled**, as it read it. A writer never guesses the generation that
introduced a change. Writes can coalesce: when two requests write
generations 4 and 5 before the controller reconciles, its next reconcile acts
on 5, and no reconcile row carries 4. The equality join above then finds the
request of generation 5 only. The reconcile at generation *G* covers every
request write of the object with a generation in (*P*, *G*], where *P* is the
generation of the same controller's previous reconcile of the object (0 when
there is none). The range join reads all of them:

```sql
WITH reconciles AS (
  SELECT controller, uid, gen,
         lagInFrame(gen, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY controller, uid ORDER BY gen
                                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS prev_gen
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT ScopeName AS controller,
           LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid'] AS uid,
           toInt64(LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.generation']) AS gen
    FROM default.krateo_audit
    WHERE LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid'] != ''
      AND LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.generation'] != ''
  )
)
SELECT r.controller, r.uid, r.gen AS reconciled_generation,
       toInt64(h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation']) AS written_generation,
       h.LogAttributes['user.name']  AS actor,
       h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.on_behalf_of.user.name'] AS on_behalf_of,
       h.LogAttributes['session.id'] AS session
FROM reconciles AS r
INNER JOIN default.krateo_audit AS h
   ON h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.uid'] = r.uid
WHERE h.ScopeName = 'github.com/krateo-platformops/snowplow/audit'
  AND h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.outcome'] = 'success'
  AND h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.dry_run'] != 'true'
  AND h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation'] != ''
  AND toInt64(h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation']) > r.prev_gen
  AND toInt64(h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation']) <= r.gen
```

Each reconcile yields every write in its range, and the reader keeps them
all; a query never picks one write as "the" cause. A reconcile with no
write in its range acted on a generation no recorded request wrote, such as
a write made before the request writer recorded it.

**The decider of a decision.** A controller that acts on a person's decision
(an access-review Campaign's `spec.decisions`, acmp's Q6) writes no decider
key: an unsigned `reviewedBy` string is the client's word. The decider is
the actor (`user.name`, and `on_behalf_of` on a delegated token) of
the request rows the range join returns for the reconcile that acted, each
signed by the token the request writer verified.

## The content hash

`krateo.audit.object_ref.content_sha256` is the tamper-evidence anchor of a
write that creates or replaces content (verb `create` or `update`):
the SHA-256 of the object's canonical content, computed by the writer from
the request body it sends. A record pins an object by `uid` and
`resource_version`; the hash also shows what it said, after the object
is deleted, and lets an exported copy be checked against the trail. It is
optional, and never written for a credential target (above): a hash of
low-entropy secret data can be guessed offline.

The value is `c1:` and 64 lowercase hex digits. **c1** names the canonical
form below. The form is fixed: a change to it, however small, is a new
form, `c2`, so a hash stored under c1 is always checked with c1. `Check`
reports any other prefix as `bad-format`.

Go writers compute it with
`audit.ContentSHA256(group, resource, subresource, obj)`, where the target
is the record's `object_ref` and `obj` is the request body as sent (a
typed object, an unstructured map, or its JSON). It refuses a credential
target (`audit.ErrCredentialTarget`), the same targets `Check` refuses.
Any other writer computes the same bytes.

**Form c1:**

1. **The content, per kind family.** A ConfigMap (core `configmaps`): its
   `data` and `binaryData`. Any other object: every top-level field
   but `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata` and `status` (a custom
   resource's `spec`; a RoleBinding's `roleRef` and `subjects`).
2. **Plus c1's annotations**, for every family:
   `metadata.annotations` kept to `authn.krateo.io/strategy` and
   `authn.krateo.io/groups`, as
   `{"metadata":{"annotations":{...}}}`, and left out when neither is
   set. Authorization reads them, so changing one changes what an identity
   may do (AUDIT-4). Every other annotation, and every label, is not hashed.
3. **Nulls.** An object member whose value is null is left out, at every
   depth, so a typed object and its unstructured form (a
   `creationTimestamp: null` in a pod template) hash the same. A null
   element of an array stays: dropping it would move the others. The content
   is a JSON object, `{}` when nothing is left.
4. **The bytes.** UTF-8 JSON with no whitespace; object keys sorted by their
   bytes; strings with only the escapes JSON requires (`\"`, `\\`, and
   each control character as `\b` `\f` `\n` `\r` `\t` or
   `\u00xx`), every other character raw, `<`, `>` and `&`
   included; `binaryData` values as the base64 strings the object's JSON
   holds; integers in decimal. A non-integer number has no canonical form,
   and the object gets no hash.
5. **The hash.** `c1:` and the SHA-256 of those bytes, as 64 lowercase hex
   digits.

**c1's key set is frozen** (`audit.ContentFormC1Annotations()`): the two
annotations v0.12.0 declared, `authn.krateo.io/strategy` and `authn.krateo.io/groups`,
and no label. It is not `audit.AuthorizationAnnotations()`: the
authorization-bearing metadata below grows (v0.13.0 adds
`authn.krateo.io/username`), and a form is fixed, so growing it never changes a
c1 hash. A content comparator still counts every declared key; c1 may then
say "unchanged" where the comparator says "changed". Hashing another key set
is a new form, c2.

The test vector (`TestContentSHA256_Vector`): a ConfigMap whose data is
`k: <é>` and `a"b: line1⏎line2`, whose binaryData is
`logo: iVBORw==`, and whose annotations are `authn.krateo.io/groups: devs⏎ops`
and an undeclared `example.com/note`, has the content bytes

```json
{"binaryData":{"logo":"iVBORw=="},"data":{"a\"b":"line1\nline2","k":"<é>"},"metadata":{"annotations":{"authn.krateo.io/groups":"devs\nops"}}}
```

and the value `c1:e8374f859e140054ea17527c08740cd2439bc7bcad48dd777a3e3cc0921d708c`.

### Authorization-bearing metadata

The annotations and labels that authorization reads (schema/v1.yaml
`authorization_metadata`). A write that changes one, by its value, or by adding
or removing it, changes what an identity may do, so it is a content change
as the AUDIT-4 ruling counts it. **Content** is the desired state
([coverage.md](./coverage.md), boundary ruling 1) plus these, compared by
key and value: an annotation only as an annotation, a label only as a
label. Every other annotation and label is metadata.
`audit.AuthorizationAnnotations()` and `audit.AuthorizationLabels()` are generated
from this one list. plumbing's `kubeutil/content` compares by it, from
v1.59.0: `content.DiffersWith(before, after, content.Keys{Annotations, Labels})`.

| kind | key | why it is content |
|---|---|---|
| annotation | `authn.krateo.io/strategy` | the identity source a session was issued by; authorization reads it |
| annotation | `authn.krateo.io/groups` | the session's groups, which RBAC binds |
| annotation | `authn.krateo.io/username` | the exact username a session Secret holds the credential of; a reader proves the Secret is the requester's by it (plumbing endpoints.OwnsSecret), so it decides credential ownership |
| label | `authn.krateo.io/principal` | the session's principal class (human, service, agent or controller): acmp's tenant onboarding selects humans by it |
| label | `authn.krateo.io/username-label` | the session's username bounded to a label value; acmp's tenant onboarding names a tenant's namespaces from it |

Form c1 hashes its frozen two annotations (`authn.krateo.io/strategy`,
`authn.krateo.io/groups`) and no label, whatever this table declares. A form
is fixed, so another annotation or a label in the hash would be a new form,
c2. The labels' and `authn.krateo.io/username`'s carrier, the session Secret, is a
credential target, which carries no content hash at all.

## Client-asserted provenance

`krateo.audit.client.*` is what a client asserted about a write, as the
writer received it after validating it: today the portal's
`X-Krateo-Provenance` header on snowplow's `/call` (snowplow#1333). These
keys are **asserted**, kept apart from what the writer verified: none is
identity, the actor's class, the agent's identity, the outcome or the
target, which the writer establishes itself, and none is a policy key. They
are written on a write only (a dry run included), by a request or action
writer.

- `source` is required once any other asserted key is present.
- `confirmed_set.count`, `irreversible`, `sha256` and `op` come
  together; `op` is below `count`.
- When the writer rejected the header, the record carries
  `krateo.audit.client.rejected` (`oversize`, `encoding`,
  `version`, `schema`) and **no other client key**; `Check`
  reports any other one as `unexpected`. The write itself still ran.

## Kept values

A controller row (v0.14.0) for a write the controller declined: an object
already holds an authorization-bearing annotation or label with a value
other than the one the controller would write, and it leaves the value as
found. Verb `update`, outcome `denied`, `krateo.audit.denial_reason`
`kept_existing_value`, no `http.request.method` and no status code (nothing was sent). The record names the
object and, in `krateo.audit.authorization_key`, the one key it kept, as
`<kind>:<key>` (`audit.AuthorizationKeyValue`): one record per conflicting key,
never a value. The key's closed set is generated from
`authorization_metadata`. `Check` holds the pair both ways: the key without
the reason is `unexpected`, and the reason without the key is `missing`. It also refuses an `http.request.method` beside the reason (`unexpected`: nothing was sent); the verb `update` is the writer's obligation, not checked.

## Kept deletions and pruned children

Two controller rows a helm-based controller writes for the children of the
resource it reconciles. Both name the child in `object_ref` and the
reconciled resource in `cause_ref`.

- **Kept deletion.** helm declined to delete a child, on an uninstall or an
  upgrade that no longer renders it, because it carries
  `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`. Verb `delete`, outcome `denied`,
  `krateo.audit.denial_reason` `kept_resource_policy`. No request was sent:
  no `http.request.method`, no status code. The reason is the key, not the
  LogRecord body: `Check` reads attributes only, and a reader filters on
  the key. The body adds nothing the record needs.
- **Pruned child.** helm deleted a child the new revision no longer renders.
  Verb `delete`, outcome `success`, no denial reason.

The `krateo.action` literal is the emit site's own. The literals below are
copied from `contract_records_test.go`, whose tests emit them through the
real Logs SDK and check the records (`audittest.AssertConformant`,
`AssertRequiredKeysDetected`, `AssertEnumsDetected`).

The emitter, built once. `logger` is the component's
`provider.Logger("<module>/audit")`: its scope name is the population the
live queries select, listed below under "Where each writer's records land".

```go
e := audit.New(logger,
	audit.WithWriter(audit.WriterController),
	audit.WithActor("system:serviceaccount:example-system:example-controller", audit.ClassController),
)
```

A kept deletion:

```go
ev := audit.Event{
	Action:       "helm.uninstall",
	Verb:         "delete",
	Outcome:      audit.OutcomeDenied,
	DenialReason: audit.DenialReasonKeptResourcePolicy,
	// No request was sent: no HTTPMethod, no StatusCode. No Message: the
	// reason is DenialReason, not the body.

	// object_ref: the child helm kept.
	Namespace:  "example-ns",
	Version:    "v1",
	Resource:   "persistentvolumeclaims",
	Kind:       "PersistentVolumeClaim",
	ObjectName: "example-data",
	Preview:    audit.PreviewFalse, // the Namespace's krateo.io/purpose label, read from the apiserver

	// cause_ref: the resource whose reconcile declined the delete.
	Cause: audit.CauseRef{
		Group:      "composition.krateo.io",
		Version:    "v1-2-0",
		Resource:   "exampleapps",
		Namespace:  "example-ns",
		Name:       "example-composition",
		UID:        "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000c1",
		Generation: 5,
	},
}
```

A pruned child:

```go
ev := audit.Event{
	Action:     "helm.upgrade",
	Verb:       "delete",
	HTTPMethod: "DELETE",
	Outcome:    audit.OutcomeSuccess,
	// StatusCode: the apiserver's answer, when the client returns it.

	// object_ref: the child helm deleted.
	Namespace:  "example-ns",
	Group:      "apps",
	Version:    "v1",
	Resource:   "deployments",
	Kind:       "Deployment",
	ObjectName: "example-worker",
	// ObjectUID: the child's uid, when the controller knows it.
	Preview: audit.PreviewFalse,

	// cause_ref: the resource whose reconcile pruned the child, at the
	// generation it reconciled.
	Cause: audit.CauseRef{
		Group:      "composition.krateo.io",
		Version:    "v1-2-0",
		Resource:   "exampleapps",
		Namespace:  "example-ns",
		Name:       "example-composition",
		UID:        "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000c1",
		Generation: 4,
	},
}
```

## v0.3 keys (migration window W1)

Written side by side with their replacement by v0.4.x and v0.5.x, with the
same value, and removed by the release that closes W1, once the data shows no
row and no reader still needs them. Readers `coalesce` the two until the
last row without `krateo.audit.schema_version` expires. `Emit` adds the ones marked
"yes"; the others it writes only when the caller sets them.

| v0.3 key | replaced by | added by `Emit` |
|---|---|---|
| `outcome` | `krateo.audit.outcome` | yes |
| `enduser.id` | `user.name` | no: only where it is written today |
| `k8s.resource.group` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.api_group` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.version` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.api_version` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.resource` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.subresource` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.subresource` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.kind` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.kind` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.name` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.name` | yes |
| `k8s.object.uid` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.uid` | yes |
| `k8s.object.generation` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.generation` | yes |
| `k8s.object.resource_version` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource_version` | yes |

## Emit never drops a record

A record missing a key its writer must write is emitted without it, and
`krateo.audit.incomplete` names the missing key's marker (for a record with no
actor: `actor`). Each marker is counted under
`krateo.audit.records.incomplete{marker}`. `Check` reports such a key as
`incomplete`.

## Where each writer's records land

| instrumentation scope | writer | who |
|---|---|---|
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/snowplow/audit` | `request` | snowplow (H, and T for an agent going through /call) |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/authn/audit` | `request` | authn's login and /delegate records |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/authn/audit/controller` | `controller` | authn's background credential writes (certificate renewal, the step-up Secret sweep, the startup identity backfill) |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/observability/gateway-audit` | `gateway` | the collector's gateway-audit projection |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/access-review/audit` | `controller` | access-review |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/identity-lifecycle/audit` | `controller` | identity-lifecycle |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/audit` | `controller` | access-review and identity-lifecycle before each moved to its own scope (split by ServiceName); kept for their historical rows |
| `rest-dynamic-controller/audit` | `controller` | rest-dynamic-controller |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/composition-dynamic-controller/audit` | `controller` | the composition-dynamic-controller's helm writes to a Composition's children (one record per child installed, upgraded, pruned or kept) |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/core-provider/audit` | `controller` | core-provider's *.krateo.io spec writes (authn mapping, spoke mirror Compositions, hub delete) and its RBAC and credential-Secret writes |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/oasgen-provider/audit` | `controller` | oasgen-provider's RBAC (rbac.apply, rbac.delete) and admission-policy (admissionpolicy.apply) writes |
| `request` | `gateway` | the agent gateway's pre-2026-10-22 access-log rows (pre-schema, the positive control) |

- `rest-dynamic-controller/audit`: rest-dynamic-controller's bare scope, with no module path, is a historical exception, kept so its rows stay selectable. Every new scope is the emitting module's path plus /audit (github.com/krateo-platformops/<module>/audit).
- `github.com/krateo-platformops/composition-dynamic-controller/audit`: The composition-dynamic-controller runs one Deployment per CompositionDefinition version, each with its own ServiceName, and every one emits on this scope: select its rows by scope, not by ServiceName.
